newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- JAN 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- JAN 10.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--The fall of inflation at all costs has been adopted as the leading economic priority by the government and the Bank of Greece. At yesterday's meeting between National Economy Minister Yannos Papandoniou and Bank of Greece Governor Lucas Papademos, it was decided that exchange and monetary policy would be directed to achieving an ambition 4.5 percent inflation rate for the end of 1997.

--The US made a quick turn around yesterday, warning Turkey off Turkey its threats to attack Cyprus, despite having encouraged Ankara's aggressiveness in the first place. Earlier Prime Minister Costas Simitis called for calm and prudence to defuse the climate created by recent comments by Defence Minister Akis Tsohatzopoulos.
--Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos will visit Belgrade over the weekend to mediate to defuse the crisis in relations between Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic and opposition parties.
--Major changes are being noted in the air transport sector as major international airline companies cut back on flights to Greece to reduce operating costs.
--Intrasoft clinches a 3.4 billion drachma deal with the European Commission to service its LAN and WAN computer networks, beating out such major players as Siemens, Digital and Bull.

--The night brought with it a sudden change in the scene, with the US warning Turkey against a threatened attack. The Turks are now threatening a blockade of Cyprus similar to the US blockade on Cuba.

--The never-ending saga of the conservative opposition New Democracy continues, but at lower levels. Yesterday's meeting however still saw volleys launched at leading figures such as former premier Constantine Mitsotakis.

--Simitis and Tsohatzopoulos locked horns over how to deal with foreign policy at the meeting yesterday: both agreed on the need for cool heads but Tsohatzopoulos wanted to stress the need to acknowledge real dangers.

--Banks are sending encouraging messages to prospective house owners and those with variable interest loans, as the Commercial Bank cut mortgage lending to 15.0 percent and the Bank of Attica by 200 basis points. Another wave of rate cuts is expected, with reports saying the rate may fall to 13.0 percent by the end of the year.
--The alarm bells sound over the flu epidemic sweeping through neighbouring Former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia (FYROM).
--Crime by foreigners has increased while the countryside has also seen an increase in murder and rape, according to a new survey. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
